tagline: A ridge road between reservoirs, past former towns and restored prairie.
intro: Woodlands Trace runs 43 miles through Land Between the Lakes, following rolling terrain along the ridge between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley. FHWA describes this National Scenic Byway as an easy drive, allowing an hour and a half for the road itself and a day for exploring. Its account emphasizes forest trails, bays, a planetarium and an 1850s farm, with a summer canopy giving way to more open forest views in winter.

Before the reservoirs, the land lay between the Tennessee and Cumberland rivers. The recreation project required residents to leave communities including Golden Pond, Model and Tharpe, even though not all the land would be flooded. Tennessee’s State Route 49 became The Trace, short for Buffalo Trace, recalling paths developed from seasonal bison migrations. The recreation area was designated in 1963; prairie restoration began in the 1970s, using fire and reseeding before elk and bison were brought in.

Start at Grand Rivers and head south toward Dover. The northern Kentucky Lake Drive offers overlooks before the journey reaches Golden Pond and the Elk & Bison Prairie. Farther south, the Homeplace and South Bison Range lie near the former community of Model; the Trace continues past the Tharpe area toward Dover.

moments.title: Grand Rivers
moments.text: Grand Rivers occupies an isthmus between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, where the Cumberland and Tennessee rivers once came closest together. Before the reservoirs, Thomas W. Lawson tried to turn local iron deposits into a major steel industry. The expanded community incorporated as Grand Rivers in 1890, but the industrial venture failed within a few years. The Army Corps of Engineers impounded Lake Barkley in 1966, completing another transformation of the river landscape. The two lakes now connect by a canal above Barkley Dam. From this northern starting point, the Trace leads south into the recreation area.

moments.title: Golden Pond
moments.text: Golden Pond’s name remains in the recreation area’s mailing address, but its residents were displaced. The Tennessee Valley Authority opened its first Land Between the Lakes office here in 1964; the last townspeople left in 1969. The site now holds recreation-area headquarters and a planetarium. At the Elk & Bison Prairie, animals roam within a 700-acre enclosure of native grassland, viewed from a paved loop road. Prescribed burning and reseeding helped expand remnant prairie before elk and bison were introduced. Grazing by those animals helps limit the growth of trees in the enclosure.

moments.title: The Homeplace
moments.text: The Homeplace presents an 1850s farm through period crops, animals and 14 original buildings. It was developed as a living museum for the recreation area, with staff in period clothing using agricultural techniques from the period. The farm and a bison range were added in the 1970s. They lie near the former community of Model, whose stretch of road was once signed Tennessee State Route 49. The Forest Service operates both the farm and the nearby bison attraction. Across the Trace from the Homeplace, the South Bison Range provides another place to observe the animals.
moments.notice: The farm includes period crops and animals among 14 original buildings.

practical: Golden Pond: The Elk & Bison Prairie’s 3.5-mile paved loop requires an enclosed vehicle. Pedestrians, motorcycles and bicycles are not allowed. (checked 2026-10-11)
